criteria.note: Read plugin/templates/scripts/runners/db/warp_db_runner.py and independently drove it. It reads the journey JSON (ordered migrations with id/up/down, optional seed, invariants of name+query+expect_rows, budgets of name+query+max_seconds), snapshots the baseline schema from sqlite_master, applies each up in order, seeds, asserts invariants then budgets, then (unless check_reversibility false) applies each down in reverse and diffs the schema back to baseline. Real stdlib sqlite3: pass fixture printed the full ordered trace 'PASS up 0001_create_users ... PASS reversibility' and exit=0; a bad-SQL journey exited 1 naming the offending statement ('up m1: statement 1 failed (near "THIS": syntax error)'). Exit 0 all-hold, exit 1 first-failure-named confirmed.

Independently reproduced every failure mode. Invariant mismatch named the observed rows: "invariant 'cnt': expected rows [[9]], got [[2]]". A max_seconds 0.0 budget failed: "budget 'b': 0.0000s exceeds budget 0.0s". SQL errors surfaced the real sqlite message and were named at invariant/budget/apply level ("no such table: missing_table", "UNIQUE constraint failed: u.email" on a seed, "near BOGUS: syntax error" in an up, and a bad down named 'down m1'), never a silent pass or uncaught crash. Asymmetric down named the residual ('b' / 'audit_log'). check_reversibility default-on; with it false the downs+reversibility step are skipped (steps show only up+invariant) yet a failing invariant STILL fails (passed False), so it is an honest per-journey escape hatch for irreversible data migrations, not a bypass of invariants.

Ran both shipped fixtures via CLI. pass.journey.json (two reversible migrations create users + a UNIQUE index, seed 2 rows, row-count + distinctness invariants + a PK-lookup 0.5s budget, clean reversal) exited 0. fail.journey.json (up creates users AND audit_log, down drops only users) exited 1 with 'down did not restore the baseline schema: residual table \'audit_log\' remains after down'. bash test_db_runner.sh (self-contained, in-memory) reported 'db runner self-test: pass'.

Ran python3 scripts/selftest.py -> 'selftest: 198 passed, 0 failed'. The db block runs against an in-memory sqlite database and drives both fixtures (pass -> passed True/all steps ok; fail -> passed False with 'audit_log' named) plus exercises every pure helper for both outcomes (check_invariant match/mismatch-with-observed-rows/SQL-error, check_budget within/exceeded/SQL-error, schema_diff identical/residual/missing, _apply fail-loud, run with no migrations). +14 expect() over the parent; the selftest.py diff is purely additive (0 deletion lines), so all prior cases are preserved. Gate GREEN.

Case-insensitive grep of the runner, fixtures, wrapper and README for bcengi/dejitech/travelpass/workpass/agentpass/coreconnect/onesim/mvne/dmitry/tripdesk/daybook/stripe/hubspot/ava = clean. .warp/capabilities.yaml declares db_migration_runner status: reference (not mechanical), and .warp/capabilities.yaml and plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml are byte-identical (both sha256 13f2c18d2daecaac0486a66aafd3849da40cb3af71eda54895fd68eff3c30469). No em-dash/en-dash/double-hyphen in the added content (the only '---' hits are YAML front-matter delimiters in the spec and a pre-existing '# ---' selftest section-separator convention, 18 before / 19 after). ./scripts/verify.sh printed 'GATE: GREEN (dea0f5f...)' with docs/secret/template-sync all pass and the reference runner correctly counted not-applicable (not run in the home gate).

findings.text: On a file-backed db (the [db_path]/DB_PATH override) the runner never calls conn.commit(), so changes roll back when the connection closes. This is non-destructive (a scratch copy is left byte-unchanged) and does not affect verification, which runs invariants/budgets/reversibility on the same open connection where uncommitted DDL/DML is visible. Observed: after a file-db run the seeded row was absent from a fresh connection. Informational, not a defect for the runner's purpose.

An invariant lacking expect_rows (or a budget lacking max_seconds) does not fail as malformed; it degrades to a 'query executes without error' check (returns no failures). The comparison guards are 'expect is not None' / 'limit is not None'. A bad query still errors and is named. All shipped fixtures and the selftest always supply expect_rows/max_seconds, so no declared check is weakened and no AC is affected; a stricter version could reject a malformed invariant/budget outright.

summary: Independently reran everything against HEAD dea0f5f (confirmed unchanged before and after). selftest is 198 passed / 0 failed with the db block exercising a real in-memory sqlite database; the shipped pass fixture exits 0 with a clean up/seed/invariant/budget/down/reversibility trace and the fail fixture exits 1 naming residual table 'audit_log'; the wrapper self-test passes. Adversarially I confirmed the runner is not a rubber stamp: a wrong expected-rows invariant fails reporting the observed rows, a 0.0s budget fails with the measured time, SQL errors surface real sqlite messages as named failures at the exact migration/statement/invariant/budget, an asymmetric or no-op down is caught by reversibility naming the residual object while a symmetric down passes, sqlite auto-indexes are filtered so an index round-trips cleanly yet a genuinely residual index on a surviving table IS named, and check_reversibility:false honestly skips only the reversal while still enforcing invariants. It genuinely drives sqlite (UNIQUE constraint enforced, aggregates computed over real rows, real error text). Genericity, dash hygiene, and byte-identical capabilities template sync all hold, verify.sh prints GATE: GREEN at dea0f5f, and the proof digest recomputes to exactly sha256:c18893a8caabed4d with the manifest bound to dea0f5f. Two non-blocking notes (no file-db commit; lenient handling of a malformed invariant/budget) do not make any acceptance criterion untrue. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
